purpose: Q-012 timed one-dataset prototype of the FULL working likelihood (finite contract with Amendment 1), after the component check (Codex 76/1709, 76/1720). Frozen before execution, 16 October 2026. Measures cost and checks the cohort normaliser; it does not estimate power, coverage or recovery.
time: Forward time u = 75 - t_Ma (Myr); boundary c = 75 - 66.05 = 8.95; horizon u = 75 (0 Ma)

generator.h0_note: Marginal extinctions per lineage-Myr by 3-Myr bin (0-3 Ma first) from lineage_events.tsv; the four bins older than 63 Ma, with no recorded extinctions, take the overall marginal rate 0.065 as a declared floor
generator.generator_k_note: The generator uses k = 1 (piecewise-exponential termination); the estimator still estimates k

observation.E_observed_value: the true bin value (no measurement noise in this prototype)

compute_limit.rule: One fit only, with a hard 20-minute timeout. A timeout is recorded as the result (the prototype is then too slow for this machine at these settings), not retried with a larger limit.

deviation: Declared after the first checks, before any fit: the frozen seed 20261017 gave only 62 recorded lineages (real tree 268), unrepresentative for COST. Over 300 seeds the reference generator gives a median of 94 recorded lineages (5-95%: 35-241; 4.3% >= 268), so marginal-rate matching does not reproduce the realised tree size. For costing only, the timed fit uses the first seed from 20261017 upward whose recorded tree has 240-300 lineages: 20261060 (264 recorded; 43 seeds skipped). No inference is drawn from this fit.

v2.note: Work item (a) after Codex 76/1737, frozen before the v2 fit: adaptive Gauss-Hermite cohort normaliser (40 nodes; precision gate log error <= 1e-4 and derivative error <= 1e-3 against a dense Simpson reference at central, stress and 40 saved v1 states), non-centred baseline random walk (prior unchanged), vectorised segment sums, and shared-event rounding. Same dataset (fit_seed) and the same sampler settings and 1,200 s limit as v1. v1 files (model.stan, checks.json, fit_result.json) are preserved.

v3.note: Solver step approved by Codex (76/1742), frozen before the v3 fit: cohort modes by Stan solve_newton_tol (step_tol 1e-10, f_tol 1e-8, max_steps 200) with explicit post-solve checks (finite values, score infinity norm <= 1e-8, curvature-scaled Newton correction <= 1e-8 max(1, |mode|)); 40-node AGH unchanged; same dataset (fit_seed 20261060 at the original lambda0 0.0708), sampler (4 chains, 1000+1000, seed 77017, adapt_delta 0.99, max_treedepth 12) and 1,200 s hard limit; one fit, no retry. v1 and v2 outputs preserved.
v3.amendment: Declared before the fit, after the first prefit check: at Codex's starting tolerances (1e-10, 1e-8) the explicit post-solve check rejected a converged-by-KINSOL mode (Newton correction 2.7e-8 > 1e-8): with small curvature (large sigma) a score residual of 1e-8 implies a correction above 1e-8. The explicit checks are unchanged (threshold now a separate fixed datum, 1e-8); only the solver's own tolerances are tightened to step 1e-12, score 1e-11; stability compared with 1e-14 / 1e-13.

v4.note: Robustness repair approved by Codex (76/1745), frozen before any v4 check: both cohort mode solves use solve_powell_tol (relative solution tolerance 1e-12, Euclidean residual tolerance 1e-11, at most 200 function evaluations), whose evaluation-limit and residual failures are domain errors. Guards in order: finite inputs, derived variances (sigma^2, sigma^2(1-rho^2)) and initial score; returned mode and score; residual <= check_tol; finite positive-definite precision; finite Newton correction <= check_tol max(1, |mode|); finite factor. Each failure is a labelled rejection. Model, priors, dataset (fit_seed 20261060 at lambda0 0.0708), 40-node AGH, sampler (4 chains, 1000+1000, seed 77017, adapt_delta 0.99, max_treedepth 12) and the 1,200 s limit are unchanged. v1-v3 preserved.
v4.algorithm_changes: Declared as algorithm changes, not prior changes: (1) four frozen initial-value files (inits_v4/), centred on prior locations (normal priors: mean; half-normal sigma and tau: median; rho: 0.5) with modest perturbations; (2) initial HMC step size 0.01, below every adapted step size seen (v1 0.017-0.041; v3 0.025). The prior locations of lambda0 and b0 equal their generating values, so the starts are near the truth for those two.
v4.implementation_detail: The 2-D covariance factor is the closed-form Cholesky factor of the inverse 2x2 precision (algebraically v3's cholesky_decompose(inverse_spd(P))), so its failure is labelled.

inits.rule: normal priors: location + 0.25 * scale * z; half-normal sigma, tau: prior median * exp(0.25 z); rho: inv_logit(0.25 z); z_rw, eps: 0.25 z; z ~ N(0, 1) from numpy default_rng([seed, chain])

probes.design: 4 selected starts, 6 established points (central0, central1, stress_s3_r09_kbm15, near_one_rho_099, near_one_rho_0999_s3, small_sigma_002), 4 saved v3 states (chains 3-4, draws 250 and 750); then 93 points uniform(-2, 2) on every unconstrained coordinate (CmdStan's default initialisation) and 93 prior-scale points (the init rule with perturbation 1.0). Each point runs Stan's own initialisation (sample, num_warmup 0, num_samples 1, adaptation off, max_depth 1, stepsize 0.01), so a domain error is reported as 'Rejecting initial value' and any other exception as 'Unrecoverable error'.
probes.pass_rule: every selected start, established point and saved state initialises with finite log density and gradient; zero unrecoverable errors, unexpected exits or timeouts over all points; domain rejections recorded by cause, not counted as passes; total within 120 s

smoke.pass_rule: all four chains finish, no fatal exception, no timeout; draws have no inferential role
